lineRef.description: Lines of a file in a pull's diff, as GitHub's review comments name them.

line.description: The last line commented on, counting from 1.

path.description: The file's path on the side commented on.

side.description: `new`, the side the pull brings in, or `old`, the side it leaves, for lines it removes. Absent, `new`.

startLine.description: The first, for more than one line; no later than `line`.

main.description: Kept in the commenter's account; for a private repository, in their repo inside the repository's space.

attachments.description: What it carries beside its body: the pictures the body shows. Kinds unknown to a reader are passed over, and kept by a client changing it.

commit.description: The hex object ID of the head commit a review looked at, or that a comment's `line` is in.

dismisses.description: The review, a dev.knotless.comment with a verdict on the same pull, this dismisses, its body saying why. From the repository's owner or a collaborator, the review stops counting toward the pull's reviews, for or against it, until its reviewer reviews again; one from anyone else changes nothing.

facets.description: The accounts its body mentions, by where: written as it is, from each `@handle` outside code and links.

line.description: For a comment on a pull's diff, the lines it is on, in the file as it was at `commit` on that side.

reply.description: The dev.knotless.comment, with a `line`, whose thread this answers. An answer has no `line` of its own.

repo.description: The repository the pull or issue is on.

review.description: The review, a dev.knotless.comment, this was sent with as one of its line comments, all in one write.

subject.description: The dev.knotless.pull or dev.knotless.issue commented on.

updatedAt.description: When its author last changed its body.

verdict.description: Present on a review: `approve`, or `changes` to ask for changes. Readers take each reviewer's latest as where they stand, and none from the pull's author.

description: A comment on a pull or issue. With a verdict it is a review; with a line, a comment on lines of a pull's diff, starting a thread there; with a reply, an answer in such a thread.
